items.title: The two-sided ideal generated by the commutators of the Askey-Wilson algebra coincides with the kernel of its polynomial quotient
items.author: Paul Terwilliger
items.difficulty_reason: The proposition compares two objects attached to the universal Askey-Wilson algebra: the two-sided ideal generated by its commutators, and the kernel of the homomorphism onto the three-variable polynomial algebra (statement lines 2792-2808). The proof first observes that the commutator ideal sits inside that kernel because the target is commutative, then constructs a complement from the monomials A^i B^j C^k, which form a basis on the polynomial side, and finally shows that every word in the generators can be rewritten modulo the commutator ideal into that complement by successively swapping adjacent letters (proof lines 2811-2883). The step that carries the content is the rewriting, since it is what upgrades an inclusion into an equality, and it is done by hand on words rather than by citing a general theorem. The directness of the sum then finishes the proof. H2.
